summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: asymptotic analysis and recurrences, discrete mathematics (induction, sets, functions, permutations, logarithms, floor and ceiling, modular arithmetic, primes, gcd and the Euclidean algorithm), introductory linear algebra (matrices, invertibility, rank, Gaussian elimination, vectors and inner products), basic algorithms (grade-school multiplication, divide and conquer, number representations in binary, bitwise XOR) and the basics of Turing machines with several tapes. They have met complex numbers and polynomials, but not the FFT in depth, abstract algebra beyond basic rings or quotient constructions, number-theoretic results such as prime density, numerical error analysis, or any research on fast integer multiplication.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers reduced modulo n, where addition and multiplication of residues are well defined and units are the residues coprime to n.

known.name: Primes, coprimality and gcd
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors other than 1 and itself, two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1, and the gcd is the largest common divisor.

known.name: Euclidean algorithm and modular inverses
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is found by repeated division with remainder, and its extended form computes the inverse of a unit modulo n.

known.name: Trial division and primality search
known.gloss: Testing a number for primality by checking divisibility by all smaller candidates, and finding a prime by scanning successive integers.

known.name: Binary representation, bit strings and XOR
known.gloss: Nonnegative integers written in base 2 as strings of bits, and the bitwise exclusive-or, which is addition modulo 2 of each bit position.

known.name: Radix representation and carry propagation
known.gloss: Writing an integer as digits in some base, adding and multiplying such numbers digit by digit with carries.

known.name: Logarithms, floor and ceiling
known.gloss: The base-2 and natural logarithm, together with rounding down or up to an integer, as used to define sizes such as the ceiling of log2 n.

known.name: Recurrences and induction
known.gloss: Proving statements about all sizes by induction and solving or bounding recurrences for running time by unrolling and summing geometric series.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying integers by the quadratic grade-school method or by splitting them in halves and recursing, with Karatsuba as the standard subquadratic example.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite set onto itself, rearranging positions, and its matrix form with exactly one 1 in each row and column.

known.name: Matrices, invertibility and rank
known.gloss: Matrices as linear maps with multiplication as composition, with invertibility and the rank as the dimension of the image.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix to triangular form by adding multiples of rows and swapping rows, which computes rank and solves linear systems.

known.name: Vector spaces, bases and dimension
known.gloss: Finite-dimensional vector spaces over the rationals or complex numbers, with bases, linear independence and dimension.

known.name: Cartesian products and lexicographic order
known.gloss: Sets of tuples of coordinates, ordered lexicographically so that multi-dimensional arrays are laid out as one-dimensional lists.

known.name: Rational numbers and dyadic fractions
known.gloss: Fractions of integers, in particular dyadic rationals whose denominator is a power of two and which have finite binary expansions.

known.name: Norms, absolute value and triangle inequality
known.gloss: The size of a number or vector, such as the modulus of a complex number or the largest coordinate, with the triangle inequality bounding the size of sums.

known.name: Euler's formula and roots of unity
known.gloss: The identity e^(i theta) = cos theta + i sin theta, giving complex numbers of modulus 1 and the n-th roots of unity e^(2 pi i k/n).

known.name: Rounding and square roots
known.gloss: Replacing a real number by a nearby integer or truncating it, and square roots of positive reals.

known.name: Polynomial time and computational cost on tapes
known.gloss: Worst-case time as a function of input size, counting a Turing machine's steps, with linear time meaning a constant number of passes over the tape.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform as a known algorithm
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer algorithm evaluating a polynomial of degree below n at the n-th roots of unity in O(n log n) arithmetic operations, used for fast polynomial multiplication.
